general_tips.title: General Wheat Farming Guidelines
soil_preparation: Plow the field 2-3 times before sowing for proper soil aeration
Maintain soil pH between 6.0 and 7.5 for best wheat growth
Add organic matter — 4-6 tons of farmyard manure per acre before sowing
Level the field properly to ensure uniform irrigation
Break soil clods to prepare fine seedbed for good germination
sowing: Best sowing time in Punjab Pakistan: 1st to 30th November
Use certified seed from reliable source — 40-50 kg per acre
Seed depth should be 4-6 cm for good germination
Row spacing of 20-22 cm gives best yield
Treat seed with fungicide before sowing to prevent seed-borne diseases
Avoid sowing after 15th December — late sowing reduces yield significantly
irrigation: Wheat requires 4-5 irrigations during growing season
First irrigation: 3-4 weeks after sowing (crown root stage)
Second irrigation: at tillering stage (45-60 days)
Third irrigation: at jointing stage (75-85 days)
Fourth irrigation: at heading/flowering stage (95-105 days)
Fifth irrigation: at grain filling stage (115-120 days)
Avoid waterlogging — ensure proper field drainage
Reduce irrigation in cool foggy weather to prevent fungal diseases
harvesting: Harvest when grain moisture is 20-25% for best quality
Crop is ready when leaves and stems turn golden yellow
Avoid delayed harvesting — causes grain shattering and losses
Use combine harvester for large fields to reduce labor cost
Harvest in dry weather — wet grain causes storage problems
Thresh immediately after cutting to prevent field losses

fertilizer_recommendations.title: Fertilizer Guidelines for Wheat
general_guidelines: Always do soil test before fertilizer application
Apply fertilizers in split doses for better efficiency
Avoid over-fertilization — wastes money and increases disease risk
Use balanced NPK fertilizers for best results
Apply fertilizers in moist soil for proper absorption

schedule: At sowing: apply 25 kg N per acre (half dose)
At first irrigation (3-4 weeks): apply remaining 25-35 kg N
products: Urea (46% N) — 110-130 kg per acre in two splits

schedule: Apply full dose at sowing time
products: DAP (18-46-0) — 55-65 kg per acre at sowing
Single Super Phosphate — 150 kg per acre

schedule: Apply full dose at sowing time
products: SOP or MOP — 25-35 kg per acre at sowing

micronutrients: Zinc sulphate — 5 kg per acre if zinc deficiency suspected
Boron spray — 0.5 kg per acre at flowering stage
healthy.special_notes: Maintain current balanced fertilization. Avoid excess nitrogen.

nitrogen.total_dose: 40-50 kg N per acre — REDUCE nitrogen
schedule: Do NOT apply extra nitrogen when rust is active
Resume normal schedule after disease is controlled
products: Urea — apply only after fungicide treatment

schedule: Apply as scheduled — phosphorus helps recovery

potassium.total_dose: 20-25 kg K2O per acre — INCREASE potassium
schedule: Apply potassium immediately — strengthens plant immunity
products: SOP (Sulphate of Potash) — 35-40 kg per acre
Potassium spray: 1% K2SO4 solution on leaves

micronutrients: Zinc foliar spray — 0.5% ZnSO4 solution helps recovery
Silicon spray — improves leaf strength against fungal entry
leaf_rust.special_notes: Reduce nitrogen immediately. Increase potassium. Apply fungicide first then resume fertilization.

schedule: Do NOT apply any nitrogen while stripe rust is active
Excess nitrogen makes plants more susceptible to rust
Resume nitrogen only after complete disease control
products: Hold all urea application until disease controlled

potassium.total_dose: 25-30 kg K2O per acre — INCREASE urgently
schedule: Apply potassium immediately to boost plant immunity
Foliar potassium spray gives faster results
products: Foliar spray: 2% K2SO4 solution — apply with fungicide

micronutrients: Silica spray — strengthens cell walls against fungal penetration
Zinc spray — 0.5% ZnSO4 boosts plant immunity
Magnesium spray — helps maintain chlorophyll in infected leaves
stripe_rust.special_notes: STOP nitrogen immediately. Stripe rust thrives on high nitrogen plants. Focus on potassium and fungicide application.

schedule: Avoid applying nitrogen during active mildew infection
Excess nitrogen promotes soft lush growth favored by mildew
products: Reduce urea application until disease controlled

schedule: Apply potassium to strengthen plant cell walls
Strong cell walls resist fungal penetration

micronutrients: Silicon spray — very effective against powdery mildew
Avoid excess micronutrients during active infection
powdery_mildew.special_notes: Reduce nitrogen. Powdery mildew loves soft succulent growth caused by excess nitrogen. Improve air circulation.

variety_recommendations.title: Recommended Wheat Varieties for Pakistan
rust_resistant: NARC-2011 — resistant to leaf rust and stripe rust
Faisalabad-2008 — good rust resistance, high yield
high_yield: Millat-2011 — good yield in irrigated areas
variety_recommendations.notes: Always buy certified seed from government approved sources. Avoid using farm-saved seed for more than 2 seasons.
